claim: A productive HIV-1 infection in humans is often established by transmission and propagation of a single transmitted/founder (T/F) virus.
source: A productive HIV-1 infection in humans is often established by transmission and propagation of a single transmitted/founder (T/F) virus, which then evolves into a complex mixture of variants during the lifetime of infection.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Keele et al., 2008 in the manuscript text.

claim: The RV144 trial demonstrated an early efficacy of ~60% reduction in HIV acquisition at 12 months post-vaccination.
source: The RV144 demonstrated an early efficacy of ~60% reduction in HIV acquisition at 12 months post-vaccination which gradually declined to 31.2% at 42 months (Gilbert et al., 2011; Rerks-Ngarm et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to Gilbert et al., 2011 and Rerks-Ngarm et al., 2009.

claim: The RV144 vaccine efficacy declined to 31.2% at 42 months post-vaccination.
source: The RV144 demonstrated an early efficacy of ~60% reduction in HIV acquisition at 12 months post-vaccination which gradually declined to 31.2% at 42 months (Gilbert et al., 2011; Rerks-Ngarm et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to Gilbert et al., 2011 and Rerks-Ngarm et al., 2009.

claim: IgG antibodies specific to the V2 variable domain of the HIV envelope protein correlated with vaccine efficacy in RV144.
source: Several studies demonstrated correlation of IgG antibodies specific to the V2 variable domain of the HIV envelope protein (Env) to vaccine efficacy (de Souza et al., 2012; Haynes et al., 2012; Zolla-Pazner et al., 2013; Zolla-Pazner et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Protection in RV144 was not due to neutralizing ability but likely due to Fc effector function, specifically antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC).
source: Notably, protection was not due to their ability to neutralize the virus but likely due to the Fc effector function, specifically the antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC) (Haynes et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Haynes et al., 2012.

claim: Sieve analysis of breakthrough infections in RV144 vaccinees showed mutations in the V2 domain in the semi-conserved structural core encompassing residues 166–183.
source: Furthermore, sieve analysis of the breakthrough infections in RV144 vaccinees showed mutations in the V2 domain, in the semi-conserved structural core encompassing residues 166–183, which seems to be one of the prime targets of the host immune pressure (Rolland et al., 2012; Moodie et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Rolland et al., 2012 and Moodie et al., 2022.

claim: The Env spike on the surface of HIV forms essential interactions with its primary receptor, CD4, followed by interactions with the CCR5/CXCR4 co-receptor on a CD4+T cell for viral entry.
source: The Env spike on the surface of HIV forms essential interactions with its primary receptor, CD4, followed by interactions with the CCR5/CXCR4 co-receptor on a CD4 +T cell for viral entry (Kwong et al., 1998; Pancera et al., 2014; Klasse, 2012; Wilen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Interaction of the V2 region with integrin α4β7 has been implicated as a significant contributor in the pathogenesis of HIV-1, particularly for dissemination and gut-reservoir establishment.
source: In addition to CD4 and CCR5/CXCR4 receptors, interaction of the V2 region with integrin α4β7 has also been implicated as a significant contributor in the pathogenesis of HIV-1, particularly for dissemination and gut-reservoir establishment in the infected individuals (Arthos et al., 2008; Arthos et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Arthos et al., 2008 and Arthos et al., 2018.

claim: The V2 domain assists in co-stimulation of CD4+T cells promoting HIV-1 replication during an acute stage of infection by virtue of mimicking MadCAM, a natural ligand of α4β7.
source: It has been shown that the V2 domain by virtue of mimicking MadCAM, a natural ligand of α4β7, assists in co-stimulation of CD4 +T cells promoting HIV-1 replication during an acute stage of infection (Goes et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Goes et al., 2020.

claim: RV144 vaccinees generated non-neutralizing V2 antibodies that block interaction with α4β7.
source: Furthermore, vaccinees of the RV144 trial generated non-neutralizing V2 antibodies that are shown to block interaction with α4β7 (Peachman et al., 2015; van Eeden et al., 2018; Lertjuthaporn et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Env is expressed as a 160 kD glycoprotein (gp160) and cleaved by the cellular protease furin into gp120 and gp41 subunits.
source: Env is expressed as a 160 kD glycoprotein (gp160) and cleaved by the cellular protease furin into gp120 and gp41 subunits.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in HIV biology, stated directly in the text.

claim: The membrane-external subunit, gp120, has five conserved regions (C1, C2, C3, C4, and C5) and five variable regions (V1, V2, V3, V4, and V5).
source: The membrane-external subunit, gp120, has five conserved regions (C1, C2, C3, C4, and C5) and five variable regions (V1, V2, V3, V4, and V5) that are alternately positioned in the Env sequence with the exception of V1V2 variable regions that assemble as a single domain (Land and Braakman, 2001; Leonard et al., 1990).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: Three protomers, each composed of non-covalently associated gp120 and gp41 subunits, assemble as a trimeric spike on the viral envelope.
source: Three protomers, each composed of non-covalently associated gp120 and gp41 subunits, assemble as a trimeric spike on the viral envelope.
evidence: This is a well-established structural feature of HIV Env, stated directly in the text.

claim: The three V1V2 domains form a well-exposed 'crown' of the mushroom-shaped spike.
source: The three V1V2 domains form a well-exposed 'crown' of the mushroom-shaped spike, hence a frequent target of the host immune system.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Each V1V2 domain consists of a conserved Greek-key motif structure with 4–5 β-strands (A, B, C, C', D) forming an anti-parallel β-sheet and two hypervariable loops that are flexible and conformationally dynamic.
source: Each V1V2 domain consists of a conserved Greek-key motif structure with 4–5 β-strands (A, B, C, C', D) forming an anti-parallel β-sheet and two hypervariable loops that are flexible and conformationally dynamic (Pan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Pan et al., 2015.

claim: The human host is often exposed to a complex genetic pool of highly diverse and heterogeneous viral quasispecies from an infected donor of which only one (or a few) transmitted founder (T/F) virus can successfully establish a productive infection.
source: The human host is often exposed to a complex genetic pool of highly diverse and heterogeneous viral quasispecies from an infected donor of which only one (or a few) transmitted founder (T/F) virus can successfully establish a productive infection (Keele et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Keele et al., 2008.

claim: A series of HIV-1 viral env sequences were isolated from four HIV-1 infected participants of the RV217 ECHO project through single genome amplification (SGA).
source: A series of HIV-1 viral env sequences were isolated from four HIV-1 infected participants (referred here as participants – 7, 61, 94 and 100) of the RV217 ECHO project through single genome amplification (SGA).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Each study participant was confirmed of HIV-1 positivity just days after a negative test (Fiebig stage I).
source: Using a sensitive nucleic acid test, each study participant was confirmed of HIV-1 positivity just days after a negative test (Fiebig stage I) and none of these participants were on antiretroviral therapy during the timeframe of the study.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study participants.

claim: None of the RV217 participants were on antiretroviral therapy during the timeframe of the study.
source: Using a sensitive nucleic acid test, each study participant was confirmed of HIV-1 positivity just days after a negative test (Fiebig stage I) and none of these participants were on antiretroviral therapy during the timeframe of the study.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study participants.

claim: Env sequences were obtained at three time points, wks 1, 4 (~1 month), and 24 (~6 months) following the positive test.
source: Env sequences were obtained at three time points, wks 1, 4 (~1 month), and 24 (~6 months) following the positive test.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental design.

claim: A single T/F virus was responsible for infection in each participant as ascertained by aligning independently isolated env sequences from wk 1 plasma, which were nearly identical.
source: That a single T/F virus was responsible for infection in each participant was further ascertained by aligning independently isolated env sequences from wk 1 plasma, which were nearly identical (Robb et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Robb et al., 2016.

claim: Around 30 sequences were analyzed from each patient (median of 10 sequences per visit), with 152 sequences in total across all four patients, over a period of up to 6 months post-infection.
source: Around 30 sequences were analyzed from each patient (median of 10 sequences per visit), with 152 sequences in total across all four patients, over a period of up to 6 months post-infection.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analyzed.

claim: Most mutations in the T/F viruses are in the surface-exposed variable regions of HIV-1 trimer with hotspots in the loop regions.
source: Not surprisingly, most of these mutations are in the surface-exposed variable regions of HIV-1 trimer with hotspots in the loop regions (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A-B showing mutations mapped on the trimer structure.

claim: T/F61 showed a few dominant mutations with relatively conserved V1V2 region.
source: Of the four T/F viruses, T/F61 showed a few dominant mutations with relatively conserved V1V2 region, while T/F100 was found to be the most rapidly diverged virus with mutants appearing at as early as one wk after infection.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: T/F100 was the most rapidly diverged virus with mutants appearing at as early as one week after infection.
source: Of the four T/F viruses, T/F61 showed a few dominant mutations with relatively conserved V1V2 region, while T/F100 was found to be the most rapidly diverged virus with mutants appearing at as early as one wk after infection.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: By week 4, a major branch of diverging T/F100 viruses harboring mutations in the V1V2 domain appeared.
source: By wk 4, a major branch of diverging T/F100 viruses harboring mutations in the V1V2 domain appeared.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: T/F94 virus acquired various mutations including deletions in the variable V1V2 and V5 regions.
source: T/F94 virus also acquired various mutations including deletions in the variable V1V2 and V5 regions.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: T/F07 virus did not show any variants until week 4.
source: On the other hand, T/F07 virus did not show any variants until wk 4.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: At 24 weeks post-infection, nearly the entire T/F07 virus population made a complete shift to a single variant containing H173Y and K236T mutations.
source: At 24 wk post-infection, however, nearly the entire T/F07 virus population made a complete shift to a single variant containing two mutations, one at position 173 that changed histidine to tyrosine (H173Y) and another at position 236 that changed lysine to threonine (K236T).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The K236T mutation restored the well-conserved N-linked glycan at position N234 located at gp120/gp41 interface.
source: The K236T mutation restored the well-conserved N-linked glycan at position N234 located at gp120/gp41 interface.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: In some T/F07 variants, a 3-residue deletion in the variable V2 loop (ΔDSV) and a 5-residue deletion (ΔNTTRFL) in the variable V4 loop co-occurred with the H173Y mutation.
source: Additionally, in some of the variants, a 3-residue deletion in the variable V2 loop (ΔDSV) and a 5-residue deletion (ΔNTTRFL) in the variable V4 loop co-occurred with the H173Y mutation (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C-D.

claim: The H173Y mutation is localized in the relatively well-conserved 'C' β-strand positioned at the junction of the cationic first half and the hydrophobic second half of the β-strand.
source: The H173Y mutation is localized in the relatively well-conserved 'C' β-strand positioned at the junction of the cationic first half and the hydrophobic second half of the β-strand (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: The divergence of nearly the entire T/F07 virus population to H173Y variant coincided with a wave of H173-epitope specific antibodies produced by the host immune system.
source: This shift coincided with a wave of H173-epitope specific antibodies produced by the host immune system.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The Y173-epitope showed no detectable reactivity to H173-specific antibodies while the H173 epitope reacted strongly.
source: The data revealed remarkable epitope specificity to the V2 domain of the original T/F07 virus, but not to the H173Y variant, at 24 week post-infection. The antibodies bound strongly to V1V2-H173 and V1V2-H173.ΔDSV scaffolds but failed to bind to the Y173 variant scaffolds V1V2-Y173 and V1V2-Y173.ΔDSV (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A showing SPR binding data.

claim: The H173Y mutation is a key determinant in epitope switching at the time of virus escape against host immune pressure.
source: These data demonstrated that the H173Y mutation is a key determinant in epitope switching at the time of virus escape against host immune pressure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The DSV deletion had no significant difference on the binding of the C β-strand epitope to antibodies.
source: No significant difference was observed with the DSV deletion mutants, although it might have played an accessory role (see below).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text based on the experimental data.

claim: A second wave of antibodies with greater breadth emerged following the H173 to Y173 genetic shift.
source: Intriguingly, a second wave of antibodies with greater breadth emerged following the H173 to Y173 genetic shift and the essential disappearance of the H173-specific first wave antibodies.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The second wave antibodies bound equally well to both H173 and Y173 C β-strand epitopes.
source: Unlike the latter, the second wave antibodies bound equally well to both H173 and Y173 C β- strand epitopes, as analyzed by multiple assays including the sensitive SPR assay.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The V1V2-H173 scaffolds bound strongly to both CH58 and CH59 antibodies.
source: Remarkably, while the V1V2-H173 scaffolds bound strongly to both CH58 and CH59 antibodies, the V1V2-Y173 escape variant either failed to bind (CH59) or showed drastically reduced binding (CH58).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B-D.

claim: The V1V2-Y173 escape variant either failed to bind (CH59) or showed drastically reduced binding (CH58).
source: Remarkably, while the V1V2-H173 scaffolds bound strongly to both CH58 and CH59 antibodies, the V1V2-Y173 escape variant either failed to bind (CH59) or showed drastically reduced binding (CH58).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B-D.

claim: Moderate ADCC responses were observed against the H173 T/F07, whereas resistance to killing was observed for the Y173 mutants.
source: The data showed moderate ADCC responses against the H173 T/F07, whereas resistance to killing was observed for the Y173 mutants, with the Y173.∆DSV double mutant showing more resistance than the Y173 single mutant (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4 showing ADCC data.

claim: The Y173.∆DSV double mutant showed more resistance to ADCC killing than the Y173 single mutant.
source: The data showed moderate ADCC responses against the H173 T/F07, whereas resistance to killing was observed for the Y173 mutants, with the Y173.∆DSV double mutant showing more resistance than the Y173 single mutant (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4.

claim: Significant resistance was observed for both Y173 variants against CH58 mAb-mediated ADCC killing.
source: Furthermore, significant resistance was also observed for both the Y173 variants against CH58 mAb-mediated ADCC killing, while no resistance was detected against a negative control CH65 Flu antibody.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4.

claim: The gp16-V1V2 nanoscaffolds elicited antibody responses in mice that recognized the respective V2 epitopes in the context of gp120 or gp140 envelope protein structures.
source: First, the gp16-V1V2 nanoscaffolds elicited antibody responses in mice that recognized the respective V2 epitopes in the context of gp120 or gp140 envelope protein structures.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by the mouse immunization data.

claim: All V1V2 variant scaffolds elicited robust V2-specific antibodies that recognized the V2 epitopes in the context of gp140 Env.
source: The ELISA data showed that all the V1V2 variant scaffolds elicited robust V2-specific antibodies that recognized the V2 epitopes in the context of gp140 Env (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The T/F07 H173-induced sera reacted strongly with H173 C strand peptide but poorly with Y173 and other variant peptides.
source: Remarkably, the T/F07 H173-induced sera reacted strongly with H173 C strand peptide but poorly with Y173 and other variant peptides (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D showing SPR binding data.

claim: The escape mutant Y173-induced sera showed broad reactivity to both H173 and Y173 peptides as well as to other variant peptides containing C β-strand epitope.
source: In contrast, the escape mutant Y173-induced sera showed broad reactivity to both H173 and Y173 peptides as well as to other variant peptides containing C β-strand epitope.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The mice sera recapitulated the behavior of H173 and Y173 antibodies produced in a human infection.
source: Thus, the mice sera recapitulated the behavior of H173 and Y173 antibodies produced in a human infection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing mouse and human antibody responses.

claim: The T/F07 H173- and ΔDSV-induced antibodies reacted with autologous T/F07 Env proteins, and with clades C-1086 and AE244 HIV Envs that encode C-strand sequence closely resembling the T/F07 sequence.
source: The data showed that the T/F07 H173- and ΔDSV-induced antibodies reacted with autologous T/F07 Env proteins, and with clades C-1086 and AE244 HIV Envs that encode C-strand sequence closely resembling the T/F07 sequence.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6.

claim: The Y173 and Y173.ΔDSV induced antibodies reacted broadly with all the Env proteins tested, and more strongly overall than the T/F07-induced sera.
source: On the other hand, the Y173 and Y173.ΔDSV induced antibodies reacted broadly with all the proteins tested, and more strongly overall than the T/F07-induced sera as evident from the heat map and the summarized binding response (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6B-C.

claim: The H173 immunogen induced antibodies with narrow specificity to C β-strand whereas the Y173 immunogen induced more broadly reactive antibodies.
source: From these, it is reasonable to conclude that the H173 immunogen induced antibodies with narrow specificity to C β-strand whereas the Y173 immunogen induced more broadly reactive antibodies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cross-reactivity data.

claim: The H173 sera, but not the Y173 sera, showed significant reduction in binding when blocked by CH58 or CH59 mAbs.
source: Remarkably, the H173 sera, but not the Y173 sera, with or without ΔDSV, showed significant reduction in binding (Figure 6D–E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6D-E showing antibody blocking data.

claim: Binding of H173-induced antibodies but not of Y173-induced antibodies was significantly more sensitive to D180A mutation.
source: Consistent with the above antibody blocking data, binding of H173-induced antibodies but not of Y173-induced antibodies was significantly more sensitive to D180A mutation (Figure 6F–I).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6F-I.

claim: The presence of histidine at position 173 favors induction of CH58/59-like antibodies with narrow specificity as were elicited by the RV144 vaccinees.
source: Overall, these data suggest that the presence of histidine at position 173 favors induction of CH58/59-like antibodies with narrow specificity as were elicited by the RV144 vaccinees.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the antibody blocking and D180A sensitivity data.

claim: In H173/Strand but not in Y173/Strand trajectory, helix content increased over time during MD simulations.
source: In H173/Strand but not in Y173/Strand trajectory, helix content increased over time, though the β-pairing within the domain remained stable.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 7A showing MD simulation data.

claim: Y173/Strand trajectory displayed a dynamic and fluctuating β-strand content during MD simulations.
source: In contrast to H173/Strand trajectory, Y173/Strand trajectory displayed a dynamic and fluctuating β-strand content (Figure 7A, left).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 7A.

claim: While helix in Y173/Helix model was fully unwound during simulation, one turn encompassing residues 166–171 remained in H173/Helix until the end of the trajectory.
source: However, while helix in Y173/Helix model was fully unwound during simulation, one turn encompassing residues 166–171 remained in H173/Helix until the end of the trajectory (Figure 7B–C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 7B-C showing MD simulation structures.

claim: MD simulations data suggested distinct conformational dynamics for H173 and Y173 V1V2 domains with the latter being relatively more dynamic.
source: Overall, the MD simulations data suggested distinct conformational dynamics for H173 and Y173 V1V2 domains with the latter being relatively more dynamic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MD simulation data.

claim: Only one of the five H173-V1V2 ab initio models depicted C strand as β-strand, while the rest showed a coil plus a short β-strand or a full coil conformation.
source: It was found that only one of the five H173-V1V2 models depicted C strand as β-strand, while the rest showed a coil plus a short β-strand or a full coil conformation (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 7D showing ab initio models.

claim: Four of the five Y173-V1V2 ab initio models depicted C strand in β-stranded conformation while only one model showed this region to assume coil conformation.
source: In contrast, four of the five Y173-V1V2 models depicted C strand in β-stranded conformation while only one model showed this region to assume coil conformation (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 7E showing ab initio models.

claim: H173Y mutation causes a structural change in the C β-strand thereby altering the conformational dynamics of the V1V2 domain.
source: Overall, these models indicate that H173Y mutation causes a structural change in the C β-strand thereby altering the conformational dynamics of the V1V2 domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural modeling data.

claim: The degree of β-stranded character was identified to be much higher in Y173 variant than in H173 variant based on ab initio modeling.
source: However, the degree of β-stranded character was identified to be much higher in Y173 variant than in H173 variant.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ab initio modeling data.

claim: The observed antibody evasion and virus escape in participant 7 was due to a structural transition in the V2 epitope, from helix to β-strand owing to H173Y mutation.
source: Hence, it is plausible that the observed antibody evasion and virus escape that occurred in participant 7 was due to a structural transition in this V2 epitope, from helix to β-strand owing to H173Y mutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural modeling and experimental data.

claim: Four combinatorial gp16-V1V2 nanoscaffold libraries were constructed in the background of H173, Y173, Y173.∆DSV, and Y173.∆V1 templates.
source: Four different combinatorial gp16-V1V2 nanoscaffold libraries were constructed. Three of these are in the background of H173, Y173, and Y173.∆DSV templates. The fourth library has a V1 loop deletion
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental design.

claim: The resultant combinatorial library encompassed 54 V2-variants possibly representing the V2 conformations prevalent in the HIV population.
source: The resultant library encompassed 54 V2-variants possibly representing the V2 conformations prevalent in the HIV population.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the library design.

claim: V1V2-specific antibody titers were quantified by ELISA using the respective purified proteins as coating antigens.
source: V1V2-specific antibody titers were quantified by ELISA using the respective purified proteins as coating antigens.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental method.

claim: V1V2 antibodies were detected after prime immunization and enhanced by several fold with each successive boost for all the groups except for the negative control groups.
source: V1V2 antibodies were detected after prime immunization and enhanced by several fold with each successive boost for all the groups except for the negative control groups where no V2-specific responses were detected.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Y173-induced antibodies showed greater cross-reactivity than the H173-induced sera.
source: Consistent with the first mouse study, the Y173-induced antibodies showed greater cross-reactivity than the H173-induced sera, as shown by their binding to majority of the heterologous Env proteins.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8C.

claim: H173-induced sera strongly reacted with Env antigens from A244, 93TH75, 1086, and CM235 strains that contained similar C β-strand sequence as the T/F07 virus.
source: In contrast, H173-induced sera strongly reacted with Env antigens from A244, 93TH75, 1086, and CM235 strains that contained similar C β-strand sequence as the T/F07 virus, while showing moderate to poor reactivity with the rest of the Env antigens as depicted in the heat map (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8C.

claim: H173 antibody responses were more sensitive to mismatches in the C β-strand region than the Y173 antibodies.
source: Upon grouping the antigens into T/F07 matched and mis-matched C β-strand sequence, H173 antibody responses were more sensitive to mismatches in the C β-strand region than the Y173 antibodies (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8D.

claim: The combinatorial H173-induced antibodies were significantly inhibited by CH58 antibodies while no significant inhibition was observed for sera induced by Y173 or Y173 combinatorial groups.
source: The combinatorial H173-induced antibodies, like the H173-induced antibodies, were significantly inhibited by CH58 antibodies while no significant inhibition was observed for sera induced by Y173 or Y173 combinatorial groups (Figure 8F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8F showing antibody blocking data.

claim: Both H173 and Y173 immunotypes play a dominant role in influencing the conformation even in the context of a library of V2 variants.
source: These data suggest that both these immunotypes play a dominant role in influencing the conformation even in the context of a library of V2 variants.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the antibody blocking data.

claim: The combinatorial H173 group showed relatively broader responses than the H173 group, with much improved binding to Env antigens such as T/F61, T/F94, T/F100, MN, and Bal.
source: Finally, unlike the H173 group, the combinatorial H173 group showed relatively broader responses, with much improved binding to Env antigens such as T/F61, T/F94, T/F100, MN, and Bal.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8C.

claim: The sera induced by Y173.∆V1 combinatorial library showed strong overall binding to both H173 and Y173 antigens.
source: Notably, the sera induced by Y173.∆V1 combinatorial library showed strong overall binding to both H173 and Y173 antigens.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8C.

claim: The Y173.∆V1 combinatorial immunogens containing both the Y173 mutation and V1 loop deletion could be an effective design for broader and stronger cross-reactive V2 antibodies.
source: Thus, the Y173.∆V1 combinatorial immunogens containing both the Y173 mutation and V1 loop deletion could be an effective design for broader and stronger cross-reactive V2 antibodies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunogenicity data.

claim: The modest 31.2% efficacy of the RV144 HIV vaccine trial in Thailand was correlated with the induction of V2-directed antibodies.
source: The modest 31.2% efficacy of the only successful RV144 HIV vaccine trial in Thailand was correlated with the induction of V2-directed antibodies (Haynes et al., 2012; Rao et al., 2013; Liao et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Analysis of breakthrough infections of RV144 vaccinees showed mutations in the V2 domain of the circulating viruses, presumably selected for their ability to survive under the host immune pressure.
source: Analysis of breakthrough infections of vaccinees showed mutations in the V2 domain of the circulating viruses, presumably selected for their ability to survive under the host immune pressure (Rolland et al., 2012; Moodie et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: The C β-strand region is conformationally dynamic and can take a helical form when bound to certain antibodies.
source: There is evidence that the C β-strand is conformationally dynamic and that it can take a helical form when bound to certain antibodies (Liao et al., 2013; Wibmer et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: A pentavalent vaccine containing five Env proteins including both the H173 and Y173 variants gave better protection in non-human primates when compared to single immunogen.
source: In fact, a pentavalent vaccine containing five Env proteins including both the H173 and Y173 variants gave better protection in non-human primates when compared to single immunogen (Bradley et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Bradley et al., 2017.

claim: Responses directed to V1 loop interferes with binding of protective V2-directed antibodies to Env and promotes virus acquisition in SIV vaccinated macaques.
source: Consistent with these data is the recent report that showed that the responses directed to V1 loop interferes with binding of protective V2-directed antibodies to Env and promotes virus acquisition in SIV vaccinated macaques (Silva de Castro et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Silva de Castro et al., 2021.

claim: Residue 173 and the presence of histidine or tyrosine at this position strongly influence the local conformation of V2 domain.
source: In conclusion, our studies show that residue 173 and the presence of histidine or tyrosine at this position strongly influence the local conformation of V2 domain and this conformational dynamism might lead to virus escape and breakthrough infections.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented.

claim: Combinatorial vaccine designs such as the Y173-∆V1 library of immunogens can display a set of dynamic and flexible conformations and have the potential to generate broad antibody responses.
source: This could potentially be curtailed by combinatorial vaccine designs such as the Y173-∆V1 library of immunogens that can display a set of dynamic and flexible conformations and have the potential to generate broad antibody responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunogenicity data.

claim: HIV-1 continues to cause ~1.5 million new infections annually.
source: In the absence of a preventative vaccine, HIV-1 continues to be a global public health concern, causing ~1.5 million new infections annually (Global HIV & AIDS statistics, 2019).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation.

claim: Combinatorial antiretroviral therapy has greatly improved the life expectancy of people living with HIV.
source: While combinatorial antiretroviral therapy has greatly improved the life expectancy of people living with HIV, it does not cure the infection even with life-long adherence (Mocroft et al., 2007; WHO, 2021).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: Combinatorial antiretroviral therapy does not cure HIV infection even with life-long adherence.
source: While combinatorial antiretroviral therapy has greatly improved the life expectancy of people living with HIV, it does not cure the infection even with life-long adherence (Mocroft et al., 2007; WHO, 2021).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: The RV144 trial is the only HIV vaccine trial that showed promise after dozens of failures in the last four decades.
source: After dozens of HIV-1 vaccine failures in the last four decades, the only vaccine trial that showed promise was the phase 3 RV144 trial conducted in Thailand (Esparza, 2013; Gilbert et al., 2011; Rerks-Ngarm et al., 2009; de Souza et al., 2012; Haynes et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Dominant mutations in RV217 participants fall on the solvent-exposed regions of the Env but not on the non-exposed or buried region.
source: Surface model showing dominant mutations (blue) falling on the solvent-exposed regions of the Env (gray) but not on the non-exposed or buried region (red).
evidence: This claim is shown in Figure 2A with structural modeling.

claim: Participant 7 showed a typical pattern of viral load curve with peak, nadir, and set point representing early captured infection.
source: Additionally, plasma viral load with peak, nadir, and set point viremia shown for one representative patient (participant 7) indicated a typical pattern of early captured infection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The H173 residue is at the center of the C β-strand that contains hydrophilic and solvent-exposed residues flanking on one side and hydrophobic and buried residues on the other side.
source: Notably, an examination of Env trimer structures show that the H173 residue is at the center of the C β-strand that contains hydrophilic and solvent-exposed residues flanking on one side and hydrophobic and buried residues on the other side (Pan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citation to Pan et al., 2015.

claim: Previous X-ray structures showed that the H173 peptide epitope assumes an α-helix when bound to CH58 and CH59 antibodies as opposed to a β-strand in the envelope proteins with tyrosine at residue 173.
source: Previous X-ray structures showed that the H173 peptide epitope assumes an α-helix when bound to CH58 and CH59 antibodies as opposed to a β-strand in the envelope proteins with tyrosine at residue 173 (Pan et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2013; Ananthaswamy et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The C β-strand region undergoes a structural transition when H173 changes to Y, from a β-strand conformation as part of conserved Greek motif to an α-helix/helix-coil conformation.
source: The picture that emerges from the above data, combined with the previously reported studies, is that the C β-strand region is conformationally dynamic and probably undergoes a structural transition when H173 changes to Y, from a β-strand conformation as part of conserved Greek motif to an α-helix/helix-coil conformation (van Eeden et al., 2018; Liao et al., 2013; Wibmer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and previous studies.

claim: The H173 region is rigid and assumes a helical/coil conformation whereas the Y173 domain is more dynamic, preferring to be β-stranded and part of a β-sheet core.
source: Our MD simulations and ab initio structural modeling of H173 and Y173 V1V2 domains further suggest that the H173 region is rigid and assumes a helical/coil conformation whereas the Y173 domain is more dynamic, preferring to be β-stranded and part of a β-sheet core.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MD simulations and structural modeling data.

claim: Two of the three vaccine immunogens (A244 and 93TH023) used in the RV144 trial had histidine at 173 position.
source: In fact, two of the three vaccine immunogens (A244 and 93TH023) used in the RV144 trial had histidine at 173 position, suggesting the H173 specificity of these vaccine induced CH58 and CH59 antibodies (Robb et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Robb et al., 2012.

claim: The strong immune pressure exerted by the host might be due to the ADCC activity of the elicited antibody responses.
source: This would argue that the strong immune pressure exerted by the host might be due to the ADCC activity of the elicited antibody responses, consistent with the previous reports suggesting the importance of ADCC responses in HIV-1 infected individuals particularly the elite controllers, and the protection imparted by vaccines in non-human primates (Bonsignori et al., 2012; Excler et al., 2014; Bruel et al., 2016; Dupuy et al., 2019; Mabuka et al., 2012; Isitman et al., 2016; Pollara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ADCC data and supported by multiple citations.
